Surah Ibrahim [Meccan, except verses 28 and 29, which are Medinan; its verses number 52, 54 or 55]

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by this. ﴿This is a Book⁠⁠ which We have sent down to you⁠⁠ (O Muhammad) so that you may bring mankind out of the darknesses⁠⁠ (of disbelief) into the light⁠⁠ (of faith) by the permission of their Lord⁠⁠, ﴾ this phrase, "into the light," is substituted for "to the light." ﴿to the path⁠⁠ (way) of the Mighty⁠⁠ (Victorious) and the Praiseworthy⁠⁠ (Praised).﴾

The Qur'anic phrase ﴿Allah﴾ may be read in the genitive (**al-jarr**) as a substitute (**badal**) or an explicative apposition (**ʿaṭf bayān**), and what follows it, ﴿the One to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, is a qualifier (**ṣifah**). It may also be read in the nominative (**al-rafʿ**) as a subject (**mubtadaʾ**), whose predicate (**khabar**) is ﴿the One to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾.

Here ﴿مُلْكًا وخَلْقًا وعَبِيدًا﴾ (**mulkan wa-khalqan wa-ʿabīdan**) means: in ownership (**mulk**), in creation (**khalq**), and as servants (**ʿabīd**).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 3:

﴿Alladhina﴾ is an adjective (na't) of ﴿yastahibbuna﴾, meaning they prefer, choose ﴿the worldly life over the Hereafter﴾, and they ﴿bar﴾ people ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, i.e. the religion of Islam, ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾, i.e. the way, ﴿crooked﴾, bent. ﴿Those are in far error﴾, far from the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 4:

﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language﴾ of ﴿his people, so that he might make clear to them﴾ (i.e., so that he might make them understand) what he brought. ﴿Then Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 14, verse 5:

﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs﴾ the nine [signs], and We said to him, ﴿"Bring out your people"﴾ the Children of Israel ﴿"from the darknesses"﴾ of disbelief ﴿"into the light"﴾ of faith ﴿"and remind them of the Days of Allah"﴾ of His blessings ﴿"Indeed in that"﴾ reminder ﴿"are signs for everyone who is patient"﴾ in obedience ﴿"and grateful"﴾ for blessings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 6:

﴿And﴾ remember [when] Musa said to his people: "Remember the favour of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Fir'awn (Pharaoh), who inflicted on you the worst torment, slaughtering your sons, [the newborn males,] and sparing your women," ﴿and sparing your women﴾ (yastabqūna, i.e., keeping them alive), because of the saying of some of the soothsayers (kahanah) that a boy would be born among the Children of Israel who would be the cause of the ruin of Fir'awn's kingdom. ﴿And in that﴾ deliverance or the torment ﴿was a trial﴾, either a bounty (in'ām) or a test (ibtilā').

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 7:

﴿And when your Lord proclaimed﴾ (ta'adhdhana) made known, ﴿"If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favour]"﴾ for My blessing, by affirming the Oneness [of God] and obedience, ﴿"But if you are ungrateful"﴾ you deny the blessing by disbelief and disobedience, ﴿"indeed, My punishment is severe"﴾ — the final clause, "I will surely punish you," is implied by this, namely ﴿"indeed, My punishment is severe."﴾

﴿And Moses said﴾ to his people, ﴿If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth, all of you together, then indeed Allah is Free of need﴾ of His creation, ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, meaning praised in His actions toward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 9:

﴿Has there not come to you﴾ an interrogative of confirmation (istifham taqrir) ﴿the news﴾ (naba') i.e. the report ﴿of those before you: the people of Nuh (Noah), and ʿAad﴾ the people of Hud, ﴿and Thamud﴾ the people of Salih, ﴿and those after them, none knows them but Allah﴾ because of their great number ﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ with evident arguments for the truthfulness of [the messengers] ﴿but they put their hands to their mouths﴾ i.e. the nations returned their hands to their mouths, biting them out of intense rage ﴿and said: "We disbelieve in that with which you have been sent"﴾ according to your claim ﴿and indeed we are in grave doubt about that to which you invite us﴾ a doubt that causes suspicion (muriib, muqqi‘ fi al-rayba).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 10:

﴿Their messengers said: "Is there doubt about God, the Originator (Fatir) of the heavens and the earth?"﴾ An interrogative of denial, meaning: there is no doubt about His oneness, given the clear proofs for it. ﴿He calls you﴾ to obey Him, ﴿so that He may forgive you some of your sins﴾ ("min" here is extra (za'idah), since Islam wipes out what came before it; or it is partitive (tab'idiyyah), to exclude the rights of people (huquq al-'ibad)). ﴿And He defers you﴾ without punishment ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is the term of death. ﴿They said: "You are nothing but mortals like us. You wish to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship"﴾ of idols, ﴿so bring us a clear authority (sultan mubin)﴾, a manifest proof of your truthfulness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 11:

﴿Their messengers said to them: "We are nothing but humans like you," as you said, ﴿but Allah bestows His favour upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾ with prophethood. ﴿It is not for us to bring you an authority except by the permission of Allah﴾, that is, by His command, because we are servants who are owned and nurtured. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, that is, let them put their trust in Him.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 12:

﴿And what [reason] do we have that﴾ we [should] ﴿not put our trust in God﴾, that is, there is nothing preventing us from that. ﴿And He has indeed guided us to our ways. We will surely be patient over the harm you inflict upon us﴾, over your harm.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 13:

﴿And those who disbelieved said to their messengers: "We will surely expel you from our land, or you will return to our religion."﴾ [meaning:] "you will become" (لَتَصِيرُنَّ) ﴿in our religion﴾ (دِيننا, i.e., our religion). ﴿So their Lord revealed to them: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers"﴾ (الظّالِمِينَ, i.e., the disbelievers).

﴿And We will surely settle you in the land after them﴾ — their land — ﴿after their destruction﴾. ﴿That﴾ — the victory and the inheritance of the land — ﴿is for whoever fears My standing﴾, i.e., his standing before Me, ﴿and fears My threat﴾ — with the punishment.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** (a concise commentary by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 14, verse 15:

﴿And they sought victory﴾ — the Messengers sought help from God against their people. ﴿And every obstinate tyrant was disappointed﴾ — he lost; ﴿every tyrant﴾ — arrogant toward obedience to God; ﴿obstinate﴾ — defiant of the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 16:

﴿Behind him﴾ i.e., before him, ﴿is Hell﴾ which he will enter, ﴿and he will be given to drink﴾ therein ﴿of water of pus﴾, which is what flows from the insides of the people of the Fire, mixed with pus and blood.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 17:

﴿yatajarra'uhu﴾ yabtala'uhu marra ba'da marra li-mararatihi (he swallows it sip by sip, because of its bitterness) ﴿wa-la yakadu yusighuhu﴾ yazdaridu-hu li-qubhihi wa-karahatihi (and he can hardly swallow it, because of its foulness and repugnance) ﴿wa-ya'tihi al-mawt﴾ ay asbabuhu al-muqtadiyya lahu min anwa' al-'adhab (death comes to him from every place, that is, its causes which necessitate it, of the kinds of punishment) ﴿min kulli makan wa-ma huwa bi-mayyit wa-min warihi﴾ ba'da dhalika al-'adhab (yet he is not dead; and behind him, after that punishment) ﴿'adhab ghalid﴾ qawiyy muttasil (there is a harsh punishment, strong and continuous).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 18:

﴿The likeness﴾ (mathal) is a description (sifah) of ﴿those who disbelieve in their Lord﴾, and it is the subject (mubtada'); ﴿their deeds﴾ (a'maluhum), the good ones, is substituted for it (yubdal minhu), like charity and kinship ties, in that they bring no benefit, ﴿are like ashes which the wind blows hard upon on a stormy day﴾, violently blowing, so it makes them scattered dust that cannot be gathered; and the prepositional phrase (al-majrur) is the predicate (khabar) of the subject. ﴿They have no power﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿over anything of what they have earned﴾, i.e., what they did in the world, ﴿nothing﴾, i.e., they will find no reward for it because its condition is absent. ﴿That is the far error﴾, i.e., the ruin.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 19:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ (i.e., look, O addressee; an interrogative of affirmation) ﴿that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾ (the phrase "in truth" is connected to "created") ﴿If He wills, He will take you away﴾ (O people) ﴿and bring a new creation﴾ (in your place).

"And that is not difficult for Allah" (ﷺ-free) — here is the translation:

﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ — difficult (shadid)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 21:

﴿And they will come forth⁠﴾ before Allah, i.e., the creation; the expression here, and in what follows, is in the past tense to affirm that it will certainly occur. ﴿All together before Allah. The weak (al-Ḍu'afa', the followers) will say to those who were arrogant (alladhīna istakbarū, the leaders),⁠﴾ ﴿Indeed, we were your followers (tabaʿan),⁠﴾ the plural of tābiʿ, ﴿so will you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?⁠﴾ (the first min is for explanation and the second is for partitive meaning), i.e., will you repel (mughnūn, dāfiʿūn) from us? ﴿They (the leaders) will say,⁠﴾ ﴿If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you⁠﴾, i.e., we would have called you to guidance; ﴿it is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; we have no⁠﴾ (the min is extra) ﴿refuge (maḥīṣ, a place of refuge).⁠﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 22:

﴿And Satan said﴾ — Iblis — ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾ and the people of Paradise had been admitted to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, and they had gathered before him: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you a promise of truth﴾ — of resurrection and recompense — so He was true to you; ﴿and I promised you﴾ that it would not happen, ﴿and I failed you. And I had no authority over you﴾ — ﴿authority﴾ meaning power and capability by which I could compel you to follow me ﴿except﴾ — but rather — ﴿that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves﴾ for answering me. ﴿I cannot help you﴾ — cannot rescue you — ﴿nor can you help me﴾ — read with a fatḥah and with a kasrah on the yā' (muṣrikhiyya) — ﴿Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me﴾ — in your making me a partner ﴿with Allah before﴾ — in the world ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers﴾ — the disbelievers ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾ — a painful, afflicting one.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 23:

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever by the permission of their Lord; their greeting therein will be "Peace."﴾ "Abiding" is a circumstantial (ḥāl) clause that is anticipated (muqaddarah), meaning they will enter it intending to remain forever. ﴿Therein by the permission of their Lord, their greeting therein will be﴾ from Allah and from the angels, and among themselves.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 14, verse 24:

﴿Have you not considered﴾ (i.e., do you not look at) ﴿how Allah sets forth a parable﴾ — and it is substituted for it (the parable) ﴿a good word﴾, that is, "There is no god but Allah" ﴿like a good tree﴾, which is the date palm ﴿whose root is firmly fixed﴾ in the earth ﴿and its branches﴾ (fara'uha, i.e., its branch) ﴿high in the sky﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 25:

﴿It gives its fruit﴾ it gives its produce, ﴿every season by the permission of its Lord﴾ by His will. Likewise, the word of faith is firmly established in the heart of the believer, and his deed ascends to heaven, and its blessing and its reward reach him at every time. ﴿And Allah sets forth parables﴾ He explains ﴿for the people, that they may remember﴾ that they may take heed and thereby believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 26:

﴿And the likeness of an evil word﴾ is the word of disbelief, ﴿like an evil tree﴾ is the colocynth (al-handhal), ﴿uprooted﴾ means torn out (ustu'silat), ﴿from above the earth, having no stability﴾ meaning no place of settlement and firmness. Likewise the word of disbelief has no firmness, no branch, and no blessing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 27:

﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word﴾ it is the word of tawhid (the declaration that there is no god but Allah) ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ that is, in the grave, when the two angels question them about their Lord, their religion and their Prophet, and they answer correctly, as in the hadith of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) ﴿and Allah sends the wrongdoers astray﴾ the disbelievers, so they are not guided to the correct answer, but rather say, "I do not know," as in the hadith

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 28:

﴿Have you not seen﴾, i.e., do you not consider, ﴿those who exchanged the favour of Allah﴾, i.e., its thankfulness, ﴿for disbelief﴾, they are the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿and caused their people﴾, i.e., caused to alight, ﴿to dwell in the abode of perdition﴾, i.e., destruction, by leading them astray.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 29:

﴿Jahannam﴾ is an explanatory apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) for ﴿they will burn in it﴾, meaning they will enter it. ﴿And wretched is the place of settlement﴾, meaning the abode, which is it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 30:

﴿And they set up rivals to Allah﴾ (i.e., partners) ﴿in order to mislead﴾ (the reading is with a fatha or a damma on the ya') ﴿from His way﴾ (the religion of Islam). ﴿Say﴾ (to them): ﴿"Enjoy yourselves, for your destiny is the Fire"﴾ (i.e., your return).

﴿Say to My servants who believe: let them establish the prayer and spend of what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before there comes a Day in which there is no trade﴾ ransom ﴿therein, nor any friendship﴾ meaning companionship ﴿that benefits﴾, ﴿it is the Day of Resurrection﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 32:

﴿Allah is the One Who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth thereby fruits as a provision for you; and He subjected to you the ships (al-fulk), that they may run upon the sea⦆ (the ships, meaning the vessels) by riding and carrying ﴿by His command﴾ (by His permission).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 33:**

﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, constantly (dā'ibayn)﴾, running in their orbits (falak), not ceasing [to do so]. ﴿And He subjected for you the night﴾ so that you may rest in it, ﴿and the day﴾ so that you may seek of His bounty in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 34:

﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾, according to what is good for you. ﴿And if you should count the favour of Allah﴾, meaning His bestowal, ﴿you could not enumerate it﴾, you would not be able to count it. ﴿Indeed, mankind﴾, the disbelieving one, ﴿is [a great] wrongdoer and ungrateful﴾, much given to wronging himself through disobedience and to ingratitude for the favour of his Lord.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 35:

﴿And﴾ remember ﴿when Ibrahim said: "My Lord, make this town﴾ Makkah ﴿secure﴾, possessing security. And Allah has answered his supplication, making it a sanctuary (haram) in which no human blood is shed, no one is wronged, its game is not hunted, and its grass is not cut. ﴿And keep me and my sons﴾ distant from

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 36:

﴿My Lord, they have led many of the people astray.﴾ That is, the idols, ﴿they have led many of the people astray﴾ by their worship of them. ﴿So whoever follows me﴾ in monotheism, ﴿he is of me﴾ that is, of the people of my religion. ﴿And whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ This was said before he knew that God, exalted is He, does not forgive shirk (associating partners with Him).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 37:

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring﴾ i.e., some of them, namely Isma'il, with his mother Hajar, ﴿in an uncultivated valley﴾ which is Makkah, ﴿by Your sacred House﴾ which existed before the Flood. ﴿Our Lord, that they may establish prayer, so make hearts﴾ i.e., hearts ﴿among the people incline﴾ yearn and lean ﴿toward them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "If he had said 'hearts of the people,' they would have yearned toward it, Persia, the Romans and all the people." ﴿And provide for them from the fruits, that they may be grateful﴾. And He did so, by transporting [produce from] al-Ta'if to it.

﴿Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal﴾ [nukhfi], meaning we keep secret, ﴿and what we disclose﴾ [nu'lin]. ﴿Nothing is hidden from Allah﴾ [wa-ma yakhfa 'ala Allah] ﴿of﴾ [min], here an extra particle (zaidah), ﴿anything on the earth or in the heaven﴾. It is possible that this is part of the speech of Allah the Exalted, or part of the speech of Ibrahim (Abraham).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 39:

﴿Praise be to Allah, who has granted me, despite old age, Isma'il and Ishaq.﴾ (Who gave me): bestowed upon me, (despite old age): along with the advanced age. Isma'il (was born when he was ninety-nine years old) and Ishaq (was born when he was one hundred and twelve years old).

Translation:

﴿My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and﴾ [make] ﴿of my offspring﴾ [those] who establish it. He said "of whom" (min) to inform that Allah the Exalted had made known to him that among them there would be disbelievers. ﴿Our Lord, and accept my supplication﴾ mentioned [above].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 41:

﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ This was said before it became clear to him that they were enemies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is said that his mother had embraced Islam. It is also read as "wālidī" in the singular, and "waladī" (my child). ﴿And for the believers on the Day when the reckoning takes place﴾ "yathbut" (stands firm).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 42:

﴿Do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do.﴾ The disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿He only defers them﴾ without punishment ﴿to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ from the terror of what they see. It is said: "The eyes of so-and-so became fixed" (shakhasa basaru fulanin), meaning he opened them and did not close them.

﴿Hastening﴾, hastening (*muhṭi'īn*), is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject). ﴿Raising their heads﴾, raising (*muqni'ī*) their heads ﴿toward the sky﴾. ﴿Their gaze does not return to them﴾: their sight (*baṣarahum*). ﴿And their hearts﴾: their hearts (*qulūbahum*) ﴿are empty﴾ (*hawā'*), devoid of understanding (*'aql*) because of their terror (*li-faz'ihim*).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 44:

﴿And warn﴾ frighten, O Muhammad, ﴿the people﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿on the Day when the punishment comes to them﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and those who did wrong will say﴾ those who disbelieved, ﴿"Our Lord, delay us﴾ by returning us to the world ﴿for a near term, [and] we will answer Your call﴾ by monotheism ﴿and follow the messengers."﴾ Then it will be said to them, as a rebuke: ﴿"Did you not swear﴾ you swore ﴿before [this], that there would be for you no ﴾ the "min" here is extra ﴿passing away?"﴾ from it, i.e., from the world, to the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 45:

﴿And you dwelt﴾ in ﴿the dwellings of those who wronged themselves﴾ by disbelief, from the earlier nations, ﴿and it became clear to you how We dealt with them﴾ of punishment, but you did not heed. ﴿And We set forth﴾ (i.e., made clear) ﴿for you the parables﴾ in the Qur'an, but you did not take heed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 46:

﴿And they have indeed plotted﴾ against the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿their plot﴾, when they intended to kill him, or to bind him, or to expel him. ﴿Yet with Allah is their plot﴾, i.e. His knowledge of it, or its recompense. ﴿And even if their plot was﴾, however great it was, ﴿such that the mountains would be removed by it﴾. The meaning is that it is of no concern to Him and does not harm anyone except themselves. As for "the mountains" here, it has been said that they are literal mountains, and it has been said that they are the laws of Islam, likened to mountains in their firmness and steadiness. In another reading, the lam in ﴿لِتَزُولَ﴾ is fathah and the verb is in the nominative, so that ﴿إنْ﴾ is the light (mukhaffafah, i.e. the lightened form of inna) and the meaning is to magnify their plot. It has also been said that the "plot" means their disbelief, and this suits the second reading, ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾. As for the first reading, it fits what was recited: ﴿وما كان﴾ (and it was not).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 14, verse 47:**

﴿So do not think that Allah will break His promise to His messengers﴾ regarding victory, ﴿indeed Allah is Mighty﴾, victorious and overcoming, nothing can frustrate Him, ﴿Owner of retribution﴾ against those who disobey Him.

Remember ﴿the Day when the earth will be changed to a different earth, and the heavens [too]﴾. It is the Day of Resurrection, when people will be gathered onto a white, pure earth, as in the hadith of the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim). Muslim also related the hadith: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked, "Where will the people be on that Day?" He said, "On the Sirat (the bridge over Hell)." ﴿And they will come forth﴾ means they will emerge from the graves.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 14, verse 49:

﴿And you see﴾ O Muhammad, you see ﴿the criminals﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿that Day bound together in pairs﴾, fastened with their devils ﴿in shackles﴾, the fetters or the chains.
Their garments (sarabil, plural of sirbal) of tar (qatran), i.e. their shirts (qumuṣuhum) of tar, because it is more effective in kindling the fire, ﴿and the fire covers﴾ rises over their faces.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 14, verse 51:

﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ is related to (*mutaʿallaq bi*) ﴿بَرَزُوا﴾ ("they will come forth"). ﴿اللَّه كُلّ نَفْس ما كَسَبَتْ﴾ ("God will recompense every soul for what it has earned") of good and evil. ﴿إنّ اللَّه سَرِيع الحِساب﴾ ("Indeed God is swift in reckoning"): He will call all of creation to account within the span of half a day of the days of this world, according to a hadith (prophetic report) to that effect.

This is the Tafsir al-Jalalayn commentary on Surah Ibrahim (14), verse 52:

﴿This﴾ the Qur'an ﴿is a message (balagh) for mankind﴾, i.e., it was sent down for their conveyance (of the message), ﴿so that they may be warned thereby, and so that they may know﴾ through the proofs (hujaj) it contains ﴿that He is but one God, and so that those of understanding﴾ may take heed (yatta'iz), ﴿those possessed of minds﴾ (ulu'l-albab), meaning the people of intellect (al-'uqul).
